🧭Start Here — How Meridian Thinks
What are the three ideas I need to understand?
Accounts are where your money physically is (Checking, Savings, Cash, Credit Card, Loan) — they match your bank. Funds are virtual envelopes that say what each dollar is for (Groceries, Vacation, Car Repair…) — they never move real money. Budget categories are what you plan to spend by type each month (Dining, Utilities…). Every transaction belongs to exactly one account and can also carry a fund and a category.
How do I know whether I can afford something?
Look at the fund, not the account. An account balance only tells you money exists; a fund balance tells you whether it's yours to spend on that thing. Funds are on the Dashboard (Fund Health), the Funds page, and the Home screen of the mobile view. Each fund also shows how fast it's being used up (⏳ runway) and the sidebar warns you before one runs dry.
How does a transaction end up counting toward a fund?
Two ways: you tag it with that fund (the Fund column, or the Fund picker when adding it), or its category matches the fund's Linked Category (shown with an AUTO badge in the fund's history). Account-to-account transfers are the exception: they only count toward a fund when you tag the fund explicitly — a transfer's category is never used to guess a fund.
What does "planned" mean, and why doesn't it change my balances?
A planned transaction is one you know is coming — typically a paycheck that hasn't landed. It's visible right away (striped row, 📅 PLANNED badge) so you can plan around it, but it is not counted in any account balance, fund balance, budget actual, income total or alert until its date arrives; then Meridian posts it automatically.
What's a good routine?
Add things as they happen with Q (or the ＋ button on mobile) → post due bills on the Recurring page → glance at the sidebar alerts → do the Weekly Review on Sundays → reconcile accounts when a statement arrives → push a backup from ☁️ Sync Data every week.
📱Mobile View
How does the mobile view work?
On a phone-width screen (768px or narrower) Meridian switches automatically to a separate touch layout with a bottom tab bar: Home, Transactions, Funds, Budget, Recurring (shows a badge when bills are due), and More. It's the same data as the desktop — just a different layout — so anything you add on your phone shows up on the desktop after you sync.
What's on the Home tab?
A Net Worth card with this month's Income / Expenses / Net; your first four Accounts; your top four Funds by balance (tap one to open the Funds tab); and your five most recent transactions. If recurring bills are due, a red banner takes you straight to them.
What are the little pills under each account?
Because every transaction is linked to a fund, each account card breaks its balance down by fund: "Groceries $320 · Travel $150" means $320 of that account's money belongs to Groceries and $150 to Travel. A dashed Unallocated pill is whatever part of the balance isn't earmarked for any fund. You'll see them on Home and on More → All Accounts.
What does the Funds tab show?
One card per fund: its balance (and goal progress bar), a ⏳ runway line ("Empty in ~7 wks at this pace"), and pills showing which accounts hold that fund's money. It's the inverse of the account pills, and both are computed from the same numbers, so they always agree.
Can I add and edit things on mobile?
Yes: tap the floating ＋ to add a payment or deposit (amount, payee, account, category, optional Fund, date, memo). Tap any transaction to see its details, edit its memo, or open 📊 Insights for the payee. Due bills can be posted from the Recurring tab. Splits, planned/future transactions, refunds, transfers and editing amounts are desktop-only. Planned transactions do appear in the list with an amber Planned badge, and don't count toward the month's Income/Expenses.
Where are search, sync and templates on mobile?
On the More tab: Search Everything, Sync Data, Templates, and the full account list.
📊Dashboard
What does the Dashboard show?
A row of Quick Actions, a Net Worth hero card with a 6-month trend line, KPI tiles (Month Income, Month Expenses, Month Net, Savings Rate), then cards for the No-Spend Streak, Recommendations, Paycheck Status (when a session is active), the 6-Month Trend, Accounts, Fund Health, Budget and Recent Transactions — each with an "All →" link to its full page.
What are Quick Actions?
One-click shortcuts: Quick Add (same as pressing Q), Add Transfer, Contribute to Fund, Reconcile, Templates, 📅 Plan a Paycheck, a Journal Note, and Post Recurring.
What is the Savings Rate tile?
This month's net (income − expenses) ÷ income, colored against a healthy ~15–20% target: green at or above 15%, amber for a smaller positive rate, red if you're net negative. Refunds and transfers are excluded from income; planned transactions aren't counted until they post.
What's the No-Spend Streak?
A day is "no-spend" when you have $0 in payment transactions (transfers and recurring bills — rent, subscriptions and anything matching a Recurring item — don't count against it). The card shows your current streak, your best streak, and the last 35 days — solid green = no-spend, gray = you spent, today outlined in blue.
What is the Cash Forecast?
A day-by-day projection of the total in your checking, savings and cash accounts for 30, 60 or 90 days. It uses your active Recurring paychecks and bills, planned transactions, and (optionally) your 90-day average of everyday spending. It warns you which day cash dips below your cushion (editable, default $500) or goes negative, and suggests ways to fix it. The more of your real bills and paychecks are set up as Recurring, the better it is.
What is the Month Close-out?
A one-page recap for any month: income, spending and what you kept, vs. the month before; top categories; budget scorecard; fund changes; net worth, debt and investment change; auto-generated wins and things to fix; and a focus checklist for next month with a notes box. Completed months are saved automatically so you can compare past months. The Dashboard tells you when last month's close-out is ready.
How do Investments work?
Open Investments, add each account (401(k), IRA, brokerage, HSA, crypto…) with today's balance, then use Update balance (or Update balances for all at once) whenever you check your investment app. Enter the new balance and any new money you added; Meridian treats the rest as market growth. You get a dated history, a trend line of value vs. money put in, gain/loss per account, and a stale-balance reminder after 35 days. Totals are included in Net Worth on the Dashboard, Accounts and Reports. Balances are typed by you — nothing connects to your brokerage.
How does self-credit track a fund that is still positive?
Each self-credit fund has a restore-to level (set when you turn it on to the fund's balance, editable). Whenever the balance is below that level by more than the float, you owe the difference, you get a toast saying how much, and the fund shows “owe $X” with a payback plan. Set the level to 0 to only track overdrafts below zero.
What are the colors on the 6-Month Trend chart?
Lime = income, red = expenses, with the latest value labeled on each line. Hover a point for that month's exact number. The same chart style is used for account and fund balance trends.
What is Fund Health?
A compact list of your funds with balance and goal progress, in the order you've arranged them on the Funds page.
🔔Alerts & Recommendations
Where do alerts appear?
In the sidebar (up to four at a time) and in the Dashboard's Recommendations card, which shows the full list. They're recalculated live from your data. Click one to jump to the relevant page; click ⓘ (when present) to see exactly which transactions, bills or balances it's based on and what to do; click ✕ to snooze it for a week — it returns by itself if the problem is still true. Nothing is silenced permanently.
What can Meridian alert me about?
Overdue and soon-due bills · categories over or near their budget · funds under 15% of their goal · overspent (negative) funds · everyday funds being spent too fast · an unassigned paycheck · flagged transactions · uncategorized spending · a category running far above its usual · a small extra debt payment that would save real interest · emergency-fund coverage under 3 months · savings rate under target for several months · an account that will run short before a bill, with the specific transfer that fixes it · accounts that need reconciling · a reconciled balance that changed · subscription audit, quiet subscriptions and yearly renewals · bill price changes · repeating charges missing from Recurring · unusual or duplicate charges · money not assigned to any fund · yearly bills with too little saved · month-end leftovers worth putting toward goals · a fund Plan $/mo you aren't hitting (each explained below) · a positive-month note · and a Sunday Weekly Review prompt. Alerts are listed most urgent first (red, then amber, then informational), so the sidebar's four slots show what matters most.
What does "Bill now charges $X" mean?
The last two real charges from a payee in your Recurring list agree on a new amount that's at least $1 and 3% different from what Recurring expects (e.g. Netflix charging $17.99 while Recurring says $15.49). Because your bill forecasts, Timeline and fund reserves all use the Recurring amount, they're off by the difference. ⓘ shows the recent charges, the per-charge and per-year difference, and an Update recurring button.
What does "repeating charges not in Recurring" mean?
A payee that charged the same amount (within about 8%) roughly once a month — three or more times in the last ~5 months — but isn't in your Recurring list. ⓘ lists each with its estimated yearly cost and an Add to Recurring button that creates the entry (next due a month after the last charge). Once added, it's forecast, reserved for in fund alerts, and watched for price changes.
What are "unusual charge" and "possible double charge" alerts?
Unusual: in the last two weeks, a charge more than 2.5× that payee's normal amount (median of its recent charges, from at least four earlier ones) and at least $30 above it. Double charge: the same payee, same amount ($5+) and same account twice within two days. They don't mean something's wrong — two coffees happen — but they're how you'd catch a mistake, a price hike, a duplicate entry or fraud. ⓘ shows the transactions and a 📊 Payee insights button for context.
What does "$X isn't assigned to any fund" mean?
Your cash accounts hold more than every fund's share of them added up — the leftover is the Unassigned (a.k.a. Unallocated) amount. It fires at $100+ and at least 5% of your cash. Since funds tell you what you can spend on what, unassigned money is easy to spend by accident. ⓘ breaks it down by account and suggests which funds could use it — overdrawn funds first, then goal funds furthest behind — each with a Contribute… button pre-filled.
What does "Yearly bill due in N days" mean?
A yearly recurring bill of $100+ is due within about five months and the fund linked to it (by matching category) holds less than you'd have if you'd been saving evenly over a year. The alert shows how much to set aside per month; ⓘ gives the saved / should-have / needed-per-month numbers, a Contribute catch-up button for the linked fund, or Create a fund for it when none exists (named Bill (yearly), with the goal and a Plan $/mo already filled in).
What is the month-end sweep?
In the last six days of the month, everyday funds that hold more than they're expected to spend before it ends (balance − bills still due − the daily pace × days left − a $10 cushion) are offered as sources, and goal funds still short of their goal as destinations. ⓘ lists specific moves with Transfer… buttons pre-filled. It never moves anything by itself.
What does "Plan $X/mo, averaging $Y" mean?
You've set a Plan $/mo on a fund, but the money actually added to it (deposits, contributions and tagged income — transfers from other funds don't count) was under 70% of the plan across the last two full months. ⓘ shows month-by-month added vs plan, with Contribute (this month's remaining amount) and Set plan to $Y buttons so the goal date reflects reality. Only funds that existed two months ago are judged.
What does "needs reconciling" mean?
A non-cash account with at least five transactions that was never reconciled (and its oldest entry is over 5 weeks old), hasn't been reconciled for over 35 days while three or more transactions piled up, has five or more uncleared items older than two weeks, or has three or more cleared (C) items waiting a week to be locked. ⓘ lists each account with its reasons, the oldest uncleared items, and a Reconcile now button that opens the window for that account. It reappears monthly until you deal with it.
What does "reconciled balance changed" mean?
When you finish a reconcile, Meridian records the locked (R) balance. If that total later differs — a reconciled transaction was edited or deleted, or something was marked R by hand — you get this alert with the exact difference. Choose Re-reconcile to fix it, or This is expected — accept to make the current total the new baseline.
What are the subscription alerts?
Subscription audit: adds up your active Recurring items that look like subscriptions (by well-known service names or a category like "Subscriptions"), shows the monthly and yearly cost, the share of your income, possible overlaps (two music services, two cloud-storage plans, four or more video services), and any repeating charges not yet tracked; each row has a Pause button. Went quiet: a monthly item that's still active but has had no matching charge for 75 days — probably cancelled — with Mark inactive. Yearly renewal: an annual plan of $15 or more renewing within 14 days, red inside a week. Pausing only marks the Recurring item inactive; it never cancels the real service or deletes anything.
What is the "spending too fast" alert?
It watches your everyday funds — groceries, dining out, entertainment, and similar — and tells you when you're drawing them down faster than the rest of the month can support, before they run out. It fires when a fund will be empty before month-end at your current pace, or when its linked budget category is on track to overshoot even though the fund still has money. It reads like "Groceries runs out in ~9 days".
Which funds does it watch — and which does it ignore?
It only watches funds whose recent spending is mostly repeated, non-recurring purchases (at least four separate purchases in the last 90 days, and mostly not bills). Anything whose payee matches one of your active recurring bills is treated as a bill: bills still due this month are set aside from the fund's available money and never counted as "pace". A fund that is really just rent or a once-a-month bill is never flagged, and funds with "emergency" in the name are skipped.
How does it calculate the pace?
It blends your spending so far this month with your 90-day average to get a daily rate, multiplies by the days left, and compares that to what the fund has (after upcoming bills). If the projection exceeds the balance, the fund is flagged. For the budget side it projects month-end spending on the linked category (what you've spent plus the daily pace for the remaining days) and compares it with the budget after subtracting bills.
What does it recommend?
1. Move money. If other funds have spare cash — their balance minus what they themselves are expected to spend before month-end — it lists specific moves (funds without goals first) with a Transfer… button that opens the Transfer Between Funds form already filled in. 2. If rearranging can't cover it, it tells you plainly that the budget needs to go up to reflect realistic spending, with a suggested figure and a Set budget button for this month. If your budget already matches what you normally spend, it tells you the fund is simply under-funded and how much to add. 3. It also recommends raising a budget that you've exceeded in 2 of the last 3 months, even if other funds could cover this month, and shows a $/day amount to make the fund last.
Why isn't a fund I'm overspending on alerting me?
Check that it isn't treated as a bill (its payee matches an active recurring item), that it has at least four purchases in the last 90 days, that it isn't an emergency fund, and that you haven't snoozed it. A fund with no linked budget category still gets the move-money and top-up advice, just no budget suggestion.
↕️Transactions
How do I add a transaction?
Press N or click ＋ Add row at the bottom of the table, then fill in Account, Date, Payee, Memo, Fund, Category, and either Payment (money out) or Deposit (money in). Tab moves between cells and the row saves when you leave it. ⇄ Add transfer records a move between two of your accounts.
What is Quick Add (Q)?
Press Q anywhere to open Quick Add. Pick 💸 Payment, 💰 Deposit or ⇄ Transfer; enter amount, date, payee, account and category; optionally tick ↩ This is a refund or 📅 Planned; and press Enter to save without leaving your page.
How does payee memory work?
Choosing a payee from the autocomplete fills in the Category and Fund from the last time you used it, so a regular grocery store is a couple of keystrokes.
What do the buttons at the end of each row do?
⊕ split · 📅 toggle planned · ↩ mark a deposit as a refund · 💰 view income breakdown (when one is saved) · 🔍 show all transactions with that payee · 📊 payee insights · ⧉ duplicate · 🗑 delete.
What are Payee Insights?
Click 📊 on a row (or 📊 Insights in a mobile transaction) to see everything about that payee: lifetime spent, average per visit, average per month and how often you go (e.g. "2.3×/mo"); a trend such as "18% higher than 3 months ago" (last 90 days vs the 90 before — red is up for spending, green is up for an employer/income payee); a last-6-months bar chart; top categories and funds; and the five most recent transactions. Names match regardless of capitalization or stray spaces, refunds reduce what you spent, transfers and not-yet-counted planned items are skipped, and a payee that mostly pays you is shown as money received.
How do I record a refund without it counting as income?
Enter it as a deposit and mark it as a refund: click ↩ on the row, or tick "This is a refund" in Quick Add. It still adds to the account balance, but it's excluded from Income everywhere (Dashboard, Budget, Reports, savings rate, weekly review), and tagged to the category you originally spent from it reduces that category's spending — a $50 purchase plus a $50 refund nets to $0 spent.
How do planned / future transactions work?
Use 📅 Plan a Paycheck on the Dashboard, tick Planned in Quick Add, or click 📅 on any future-dated row. It appears immediately with a striped background and a 📅 PLANNED badge but is excluded from every balance, budget actual, fund total, income figure and alert until its date arrives, when Meridian posts it automatically. Click 📅 again to post one early.
How do I split a transaction across categories?
Click ⊕ on the row. Add as many lines as you need, each with a category and amount; a live indicator is green ✓ when the lines match the total and amber while there's a remainder. Each line counts toward its own budget category and in reports.
Can I split a transaction across funds — even a transfer?
Yes. Every split line has its own optional Fund dropdown. Leave it on "— auto/none —" and that line falls back to the fund linked to its category (same as an unsplit transaction); choose a fund to earmark just that line's amount to it. So one Target run can put $40 toward Household and $25 toward Gifts. This works on transfers too: when you move money between accounts and tag the split lines to different funds, each fund gets credited for its own line even though the transaction itself has no single fund. Fund balances, history logs and alerts all use each fund's own slice; its history shows a purple SPLIT badge.
What do the cleared codes mean?
— uncleared · C cleared (on your statement, reconciliation not finished) · R reconciled and locked. Click the pill to cycle through them.
What does FLAG in the memo do?
Type FLAG (capitals) in any memo to mark a transaction for follow-up. The row highlights, a pulsing 🚩 button at the top of the page shows the count, and clicking it opens a list where you can edit the memo or Clear Flag. Flagged items also appear as a sidebar alert.
How do I bulk-edit?
Tick the checkbox on one or more rows (the header checkbox selects all visible rows). A floating bar lets you change the category or fund for all of them, or delete them at once.
How do I search and filter?
The page has filters for account, date range, amount range and free-text search (payee, memo, category, date, amount, account). The global search bar (press /) finds transactions by number (#89, Tx #89 or just 89), or the word transfer for all transfers, and jumps to and highlights the row.
What are the colored dots next to categories?
Every category has a small color swatch (on Budget and next to the category on each Transactions row) so you can scan by color. It's automatic and stable, or set your own in ⋮ Manage Budget Categories.
Why does it say "Showing 200 of …"?
To stay fast with a large history the table renders 200 rows at a time. Click Load 200 more ↓, or narrow the view with filters. Planned rows are shown but their running balance is faded because they haven't posted.
What is the memo field?
Click a Memo cell to expand it into a text area; press Esc or click away to save. It's for a short note on that one line — use the Journal for bigger context.
How do I use Templates?
Press T or use the 📋 Templates button. Save any transaction as a reusable recipe, then click Apply to post it again.
🏦Accounts
What account types are there?
Checking, Savings, Cash, Credit Card and Loan. Assets (checking, savings, cash) are listed first, liabilities (cards, loans) below. Net Worth = assets − liabilities. Planned (future) transactions aren't included until they post.
What does the Reconcile Status column show?
How many transactions are still uncleared (⚠) and the date the account was last reconciled (click it to open Reconcile for that account). A green ✓ means everything is cleared.
How do I reconcile an account?
Click Reconcile on the account (or the "Last:" date on the Accounts page), set the statement date, and enter the statement's ending balance. Items you already marked C start ticked; tick the rest that appear on the statement (clicking anywhere on a row works). When the difference reaches $0.00 click Mark Reconciled to lock them as R. If it doesn't balance you can use Reconcile Checked ⚠ to lock what you've ticked and carry the remaining difference forward. Transactions dated after the statement date are hidden unless you tick Show items after statement date, and planned (future) items never appear.
What does ✨ Smart Match do?
It starts from your cleared (C) items, then looks for the smallest group of uncleared transactions (up to three) whose total closes the gap to your statement — or, if you've cleared too much, the one or two items to leave off because they haven't posted at the bank yet or were entered twice. It also checks whether everything through the statement date balances exactly. If you'd rather do it by hand, Check all through statement date and Clear checks are one click each.
What if nothing balances?
Smart Match then looks for the usual culprits: an amount with two digits swapped (54.30 typed as 45.30), a payment entered as a deposit (off by exactly twice the amount), an entry that appears twice, or a gap divisible by 9. If none fits, a missing transaction (bank fee, interest, auto-payment) is the most likely cause, and ＋ Add … to balance creates a "Reconciliation adjustment" entry for the difference, already cleared and ticked, that you can rename and categorise once you find out what it was.
Does Meridian remember past reconciliations?
Yes. Each finished session (date, statement balance, item count, whether it was partial) is saved, the last few are listed at the bottom of the Reconcile window, and the Accounts page shows the most recent statement date. That history powers the needs reconciling and reconciled balance changed alerts.
What's the dashed line and the pace text under each account's chart?
If an account has a Goal ($) set, its 6-month trend shows a dashed amber goal line (for debts it's on the negative side — the goal is paying down toward zero). Underneath, "📈 On pace for …" gives an estimated date, "🎉 Goal reached", or "⏸ Not currently trending toward this goal".
Can I see which funds an account's money belongs to?
On the Funds page the By Account cards show how much of all your fund money sits in each account. On mobile, every account card lists the funds inside it, plus an Unallocated amount.
Can I reorder accounts?
Yes — use ▲ ▼ on each row. The order is used everywhere, including the first four shown on the mobile Home screen.
💼Funds
What are Funds?
Virtual envelopes — earmarked money for a purpose (Emergency Fund, Vacation, Groceries…). The money still sits in your bank account; funds track how much of it is spoken for. A fund's balance = everything counted toward it (tagged or category-linked transactions) + contributions + transfers in − transfers out.
What's at the top of the Funds page?
Four cards: Total Balance (across all funds), Goal Progress, Monthly Recurring (all active recurring payments normalized to a monthly cost — tap for a per-category breakdown) and Needs Attention (low or overspent funds). Below: By Account, Budget by Group and Fund Trends, then the fund table.
What are the table's columns and the cycle range?
Fund Name, Linked Category, Goal, Spent, Remaining, Cycle Total, Progress. The From/To dates with Apply (or All time) set the cycle that "Cycle Total" covers. Expand a fund with ▼ to see its full history.
What is a Linked Category?
Set a fund's Linked Category and any transaction in that category counts toward the fund automatically — shown with an AUTO badge. This doesn't apply to account-to-account transfers, which need an explicit fund tag.
What is a fund's history log?
The ▼ button opens every entry counted toward the fund with a running balance. Badges tell you what each is: CONTRIB (money you put in), XFER (moved between funds), REALLOC (an account transfer earmarked to the fund — a reallocation, not spending), AUTO (linked by category, not tagged), SPLIT (only this fund's share of a split). Click ✏️ to edit or delete an entry. Above the log, pills show which accounts hold the fund's money.
How do I put money into a fund?
＋ Fund Actions ▾ → Contribute to Fund: choose the fund, date, amount, the From Account the money sits in, and a note. It's a virtual allocation — your bank balance doesn't change. Contributions are also created by Auto-Replenishment (below). Contributed this month only counts this kind of money.
How do I move money from one fund to another?
＋ Fund Actions ▾ → Transfer Between Funds. Choose From and To funds, Backed by Account (which account's portion of the source fund the money comes from — the list shows what each account holds in that fund), amount, date and an optional note. It's a pure reallocation: no bank movement, account balances unchanged, both fund balances update immediately, and both funds' history show a blue XFER entry.
Is a fund-to-fund transfer a contribution or spending?
Neither. It's excluded from "Spent", from the (+$ contrib) tag on the fund table and from the Contributed this month bar — moving money between envelopes isn't new money saved and isn't money spent. It does still change each fund's balance.
How do I edit or delete a fund transfer?
Open either fund's history and click ✏️ on the XFER entry. You can change the date, amount and note and the matching entry in the other fund updates with it; the fund itself is locked (delete and re-add if it was the wrong fund). Delete removes just that one transfer — not other transfers between the same two funds.
What happens if I transfer more than a fund has in that account?
A red warning shows how much that account actually holds in the source fund. You can still save it, but the source fund's balance in that account will go negative.
How do auto-replenishment rules work?
＋ Fund Actions ▾ → Auto-Replenishment Rules: under a specific account, set percentages of each deposit to allocate into funds. When you post a deposit, a preview appears — review it and click Apply. Deleting that deposit later removes its allocations too.
What is the Plan $/mo box?
On any fund with a goal, the Fund Trends card (now on the Goals page) has a Plan $ /mo box. Left blank, the pace projection uses your trailing 3-month average, which can mislead with a short history. Enter what you intend to put in (e.g. 200) and the projected goal date uses that instead; clear it to go back to automatic.
What is "Contributed this month"?
Once a Plan $/mo is set, a progress bar shows how much you've added to the fund this calendar month against the plan — net of money spent from the fund, so spending drags it down and it can go negative. Fund-to-fund transfers are excluded. Colors: green with ✓ at 100%+, blue at 50%+, amber below that, red if negative.
What is the ⏳ runway line?
On every fund's trend card (and on the mobile Funds tab): "Empty in ~7 wks at this pace ($190/mo)". It divides the fund's balance by your average monthly spending from it over the last 90 days (a young fund is averaged over how long it has actually existed). Contributions, fund-to-fund transfers and account transfers never count as spending. Colors: red under 1 month, amber under 2, green beyond. "No spending from this fund in the last 90 days" means there's nothing to project; "Empty — overdrawn" means the balance is already negative.
What is the Fund Trends card?
On the Goals page, each fund gets a 6-month balance chart. A fund with a goal gets a dashed goal line and a pace projection ("📈 On pace for …", "🎉 Goal reached", or "⏸ Not currently trending toward this goal"), plus the Plan box, the Contributed bar and the runway line.
How do I tell the buffer money apart from my spending money?
The Income Buffer is your extra paycheck in reserve: it's already in your bank account, but earmarked. It's shown as 🛟 reserved under that account's balance (Accounts page and Dashboard), as a blue-tinted Reserved row on the Funds page, as a dashed 🛟 pill on mobile account cards, and as its own highlighted box on the Steady Salary card. It's never counted in Safe to spend. Choose which account it sits in under 💵 settings → "Held in". When you want it, click Take an extra paycheck: the reserved label lifts, and (optionally) your replenish rules share it out to your funds like a normal paycheck.
How do auto-replenish rules work with steady-salary mode?
By default, with steady-salary mode on, your replenish rules apply their percentages to your monthly salary instead of each raw deposit. The first salary-worth of the month's income (in the order it lands) is allocated by the rules; anything above goes to the Income Buffer when the month ends, so no dollar is earmarked twice. The confirmation preview explains how much of the deposit counts. The Income Buffer can't be a rule target. If a month comes in short and you click Draw, the drawn amount also tops the rule funds back up so they end the month at their full share. Untick "Replenish rules allocate from my salary" in the 💵 settings to get the old per-deposit behavior back.
How does steady-salary mode connect to the Budget?
With the mode on, your Budget's income line (the category you choose in the salary settings, 💵 on its row) plans on your steady salary instead of a typed number — so Budget Income, Net (Budget) and the Dashboard all use it. A banner at the top of Budgets compares your planned spending with the salary (over-planned, or how much has no job yet), shows this month's progress and what will move to or from the buffer, and how many months of planned spending the buffer covers. Typing a number into the income line for a month overrides the salary for that month. Alerts warn when the budget spends more than the salary, or when your real spending usually does. Untick "Budget income follows my steady salary" to keep the two separate; turning the mode off puts your own numbers back (nothing is overwritten).
What is steady-salary (irregular-income) mode?
For uneven paychecks. (Nothing is ever taken out of the buffer automatically: a short month is flagged, and you choose Draw or Skip, unless you tick "Automatically cover short months".) Turn it on from 💵 Steady Salary on the Dashboard. Meridian takes your income from the last six finished months and sets a monthly salary: your lowest month (safest) or the average — or a fixed amount you type. When each month ends, income above the salary is banked in an Income Buffer fund; if the month was short, Meridian flags it and you choose whether to draw the gap from the buffer (it never does so on its own unless you tick the option). The Dashboard card shows the salary, this month's progress and how many months of salary the buffer holds, and alerts warn when the buffer is thin, income runs below the salary two months running, or your salary could go up. It's fully optional: Turn off stops everything and offers to remove the buffer entries it added. It only moves money between the buffer fund and your other money; it doesn't change your transactions or accounts.
What is "Safe to spend" on the Dashboard and mobile Home?
One number answering "can I buy this?" without opening a page. Meridian adds up the balances of your Everyday funds, subtracts the recurring bills that draw on those funds before your next paycheck, and divides what's left by the days until payday. It also shows what's left of today's allowance after what you've already spent. Type an amount into Can I buy ___? for a yes / yes-but / no. Click ⓘ to see the math fund by fund. Next payday comes from your Pay Cycle (Budget → Paycheck), else your largest recurring deposit, else your pay periods. A bill is only subtracted if it's linked to an everyday fund (by fund, or by matching category); any others are listed so you know they weren't counted.
How do I mark a fund as Everyday or Savings?
Each fund has a small badge next to its name (Funds table, Goals page cards, and the top of the fund's ⓘ panel). Click it to cycle Auto → 💸 Everyday → 🏦 Savings. Auto lets Meridian guess from your last 90 days (several non-bill purchases = everyday; funds named "emergency" = savings). Choosing Everyday or Savings overrides the guess. Everyday funds feed Safe to spend, the spending-pace alerts, weekday alerts and the month-end sweep; Savings funds are left out of all of them.
What are Trips & Projects, and how do they connect to my Budget?
Your all-in-one planner for a trip or a big project (kitchen remodel…). Create one with ＋ New trip / project, then work through its tabs: Overview (countdown, readiness, what's coming up, plan vs spent), Budget, Bookings & itinerary, Checklist (to-dos and packing), Savings, Spending and Wrap-up.

Budget tab: plan by category (flights 0291, lodging 0292, car 0293, food 0294, activities 0295… — your 029x travel categories) with an optional buffer %, or just one total. With Include in Budget on, those amounts are added on top of your regular monthly budget for the same categories, in the months the trip happens: dated bookings land in their own month, everything else is spread across the trip's days. A 🧳 +$ chip on the Budgets page shows where the extra comes from and a banner lists the trips in that month. Your own typed budget is never overwritten — turn the switch off and the extra disappears. If you type a new number in a budget cell, Meridian keeps the trip's share separate.

Bookings: add flights, hotels, tours… with a cost, date, pay-by date and confirmation #. Status goes Idea → Booked → Paid. Booked-but-unpaid money counts against what's free; 💳 Record payment creates the transaction, tags it and marks it Paid so nothing is counted twice. Savings creates a fund for the trip with a goal and deadline and shows how much to set aside each month. Spending tags real transactions (tag with 🏷 anywhere) and suggests untagged 029x purchases around your dates. Wrap-up compares planned vs actual, keeps notes and a rating, and you can duplicate the trip as a template. More: enter a booking in a foreign currency (amount + rate → converted to dollars), set a free-cancellation date (you're alerted before it ends), see a daily spending allowance while you're on the trip, split costs with the people you travel with (who paid, who owes whom) on the Spending tab, and compare cost per day with your past trips on Wrap-up. Alerts warn about payments due, trips starting soon with loose ends, a behind fund, untagged travel spending and categories running over plan.
What does the 🔍 Why? button on Budgets do?
It explains the selected month in plain English: how far over or under budget you are, and which categories account for most of the gap — with the specific payees and purchases behind each one ("Groceries was $180 over, mostly Costco $240 over 2 purchases"). It also flags new payees, spending in categories with no budget, where you saved, income vs plan, how this month compares with last month, when in the month the money went out, and your biggest purchases. For the current month it compares against where you should be today (budget × days elapsed), not the full-month budget. Use ◀ ▶ to look at other months.
What are the wish list, trip timeline, quick expense, packet and budget suggestions?
💭 Wish list: set a trip's status to Wish (or use the Wish list filter) for someday trips — give it a rough cost and a target month and Meridian shows how much to save per month; Start planning → promotes it. The home page has a 12-month timeline of all your trips. On a trip's Spending tab, ＋ Log an expense adds a real transaction already tagged to the trip (foreign currency supported — enter the rate once). On the Budget tab, ✨ Suggest from past trips turns what you actually spent per day per person on completed trips into daily rates for this one. 📄 Packet opens one printable page (route, day-by-day, bookings with confirmation numbers, documents, open checklist items, budget) you can print or save as a PDF for offline use.
How do the trip checklists, packing lists and planning tools work?
New trip → Start from a preset (beach, city, international, road trip, camping, ski, business, cruise, family) and Meridian builds a dated to-do timeline (book flights T‑90 days, check passport T‑180, notify bank T‑14…) plus a packing list sized to your trip length. Or use ✨ Build lists any time on the Checklists tab and tick exactly what applies (flying, hot, kids, camping…). Packing items have categories, quantities, an owner, and can be marked need to buy (with a cost) — the 🛒 Gear still to buy bar can drop the total into your budget. Save any list as My template, add it to future trips, and use ↺ Unpack all to reuse a list. Due dates move automatically if you change the trip's start date.

Budget tab: besides fixed amounts you can set a per day per person rate on any category (food $60/day × days × travelers), save what-if scenarios and compare totals, and see which months your remaining payments fall in. Itinerary tab: add route & stops for multi-city trips. Info tab: destination quick facts, a vault for passports, insurance, addresses and contacts (passport expiry is checked against your return date), and trip notes. The Overview shows a planning roadmap grouped by how soon things are due, and alerts cover overdue tasks, unfinished packing, gear to buy and passport validity.
Are credit card payments counted as expenses? What about other transfers?
Plain transfers between your own accounts never count as income or spending. A credit card payment is the one exception: mark it and it counts as an expense (category 0237 - Credit Card Payments, created for you — or use your own "card payment" category), while the matching deposit on the card is still just a transfer, so it never inflates income. Not every transfer to a card is a payment (a refund moved to the card, a balance transfer…), so it's a per-transfer choice: in Add Transfer the box "This is a credit card payment" appears whenever the destination is a credit card, and any existing transfer has 💳 Mark as credit card payment in its ⋯ menu. You'll also get a one-time alert to review existing transfers into cards. Heads-up: if you also categorize the purchases made on the card, counting the payment as well counts that money twice — keep an eye on your totals.
What is self-credit on a fund?
If you like to charge purchases to their dedicated fund even when it's empty, switch on 💳 Self-credit for that fund (the 💳 button on its row). Small dips below the float (default $30) are treated as normal — you reallocate those. A bigger deficit becomes a balance you owe that fund: it's shown in amber, tracked on a payback plan (a monthly amount or a “clear by” month) with a projected payoff date, and it no longer triggers “overspent” alerts, spending-pace warnings or attention counts. Nothing is taken from your other funds or goals, and Safe to spend already ignores a negative fund. Click Pay back to put money in; the balance clears when the fund is back to zero. Moves between funds don't count as payback — only new money you contribute.
What do the ⓘ buttons do?
Tap ⓘ next to Net Worth, Month Income/Expenses/Net, Savings Rate, Steady Salary, the extra-paycheck reserve, credit-card utilization or any Financial Health factor to see, in plain English, how that number is calculated — with your own figures filled in.
How is the Financial Health score calculated?
Open Financial Health in the sidebar. The score (0–100) is a weighted average of five factors: emergency runway (30%: cash ÷ average monthly spending, 6 months = full marks), savings rate (25%: 20%+ of income kept = full marks), debt-to-income (20%: minimum debt payments ÷ income), card utilization (15%: under 10% is best) and bills on time (10%). A factor Meridian can't measure (for example no credit cards) is left out and the rest re-weighted. “Since last month” recalculates the score as of the same day last month so you can see which factor moved it. It's a guide, not financial advice.
What are the monthly tips?
Once a month Meridian picks one short tip based on your own data — your largest recurring bill, a category that's creeping up, high card utilization, uncategorized spending and so on. Tap Another tip for a different one. They appear on the Dashboard and the Financial Health page.
How do Rules work?
On Transactions, click 🧩 Rules. A rule is if conditions (payee, note, amount, income/expense, account, day of week, category) match then actions happen: set a category, assign a fund, add a #tag, flag the transaction for review (🚩), or add to the note. Rules run on every new transaction and when you edit a payee or amount, in the order listed (use ↑ ↓). By default they only fill in blanks — tick “Overwrite” on a rule to replace an existing category or fund. Use Preview matches while editing and Run on past transactions… to apply rules to history. Transfers are never touched. Click a #tag chip under a payee to see everything with that tag.
How does credit card utilization work?
On Accounts, click 💳 on a credit card and enter its limit, statement day, due day and (optionally) rewards %. The card's progress bar then shows utilization (balance ÷ limit) with a marker at 30%. Meridian alerts you as you near 30%, and again at 30%, 50% and 75%. It also works out the best day to pay: card issuers usually report your balance on the statement date, so paying a couple of days before it closes keeps the reported balance low. The suggested amount accounts for what you usually spend on the card between now and the close. If the last statement isn't fully paid, you get a reminder before the due date. Rewards shows this year's purchases × your rate, net of refunds.
What does the ⓘ button on a fund show?
Click ⓘ on a fund's trend card (or in its table row) for the full story: why it shows its target date (the exact math — remaining amount ÷ your Plan $/mo, or the average net change of the last three months with each month's added/spent split — plus what it would take to finish in 6, 12 or 24 months); a 12-month balance chart; money in vs out by month; the categories and payees that pull the most from the fund (switch between 30 days, 90 days, 1 year and all time, with ▲/▼ change versus the previous period); and a spending trend with average purchase, largest purchase and busiest weekday. It also explains why a date may look late — for example, this month is only partly over, or spending is eating a large share of what you add. Transfers between funds and planned future items are not counted as spending.
How do target dates and the Goals page work?
Give any fund goal (on its trend card, its ⓘ panel, or the Goals page) a deadline. Meridian then shows the monthly amount needed (still to go ÷ months left), compares it with your pace (your Plan $/mo, or the last three months' average net change), and measures you against a straight-line schedule from the day you set the date — the dashed marker on the progress bar. If you're short you'll get a behind schedule alert with one-click fixes: set the Plan to the needed amount, or move the deadline to the projected finish. The Goals page (sidebar) lists every fund and savings-account goal with progress, deadline, needed vs pace, projected date and status, totals needed vs saved per month, and a what-if slider that adds extra money per month (deadline gaps first) and shows the new projected dates. Debts are on the Debt Payoff page instead.
What are milestones and streaks?
Every goal has 25%, 50%, 75% and 100% markers on its progress bar (filled in once passed, with the date shown in the fund's ⓘ panel and on the Goals page). Crossing one in the last three weeks triggers a celebratory note in your alerts. The 🔥 streak counts consecutive complete months you met your Plan $/mo — or simply grew the goal, if no plan is set.
What does the ⓘ on a budget category show?
On the Budget page (and next to each category in the Dashboard's budget card), ⓘ explains that category for the selected month: budget vs actual and a month-end projection, then a plain-language why it's over or under — compared with the previous three months, whether one big transaction, more frequent purchases or bigger ones, or new payees drove it, and whether the budget itself looks too low (over in most recent months). It also shows a 12-month spent-vs-budget chart, the payees it goes to (this month, 90 days, a year or all time, with ▲/▼ versus the previous period), the largest purchases, and a one-click Set next month's budget suggestion.
What is the weekday-pattern alert?
If most of an everyday fund's non-bill spending over the last 90 days lands on weekends (55% or more) or on a single weekday (40% or more), you'll get an alert with a weekday chart and a suggested weekly allowance — the fund's available balance after bills due, divided by the weeks left in the month, with the weekend slice broken out. It turns amber when your usual weekly spending is above that allowance. The same chart appears under When the money goes out in a fund's ⓘ panel.
What is "By Account"?
One card per account showing the total of fund money held there — e.g. "$800 of funds in Checking, $1,200 in Savings". The same numbers drive the per-fund account pills in the history log and on mobile.
What does intra-fund transfer / REALLOC mean?
Moving cash between two real accounts while keeping it earmarked to the same fund (checking → cash for the gas fund) isn't spending, so it's excluded from "Spent" and shown as REALLOC.
Can I reorder funds?
Yes — ▲ ▼ in each fund row. The order carries to Fund Health, dropdowns and the Funds page. Accounts and budget categories reorder the same way; ⋮ Manage Budget Categories also supports drag-and-drop.
🎯Budget
How is the budget structured?
Categories use a 4-digit code: 01xx = Income, 02xx = Expenses; the 3rd digit is the group (021 Housing, 022 Utilities, 025 Vehicle…); the 4th is the line item. You can search at group (029) or line (0291) level.
What is budget rollover?
Tick Rollover on an expense category and any unspent amount carries into next month's budget for it ($200 budget, $150 spent → next month $250).
How do I freeze a month?
Click 🔓 Freeze Month next to the month picker to lock that month's budget and actuals as a permanent record; the row shows 🔒 and stops being editable, so later budget changes can't rewrite history (and year-over-year comparisons stay accurate). 🔒 Unfreeze Month undoes it.
What is the Uncategorized row?
An amber ⚠ row appears when expenses have no category; click view to filter to them. Uncategorized spending isn't counted in any budget.
Do splits and refunds count?
Yes — each split line counts toward its own category in the monthly view, yearly grid, dashboard card and drill-down; refunds reduce the category they're tagged to. Planned (future) transactions don't count until they post.
How does the Yearly view work?
Toggle Budget / Actual / Difference. In Difference, positive = surplus (under budget on expenses, over on income) in green; negative = deficit in red.
What is the Next Mo. Forecast column?
A suggested budget for next month from a weighted average of the last 3 months' actual spending (most recent weighs most), with a ▲/▼ badge when it differs by more than 5%. It only changes anything when you click Use for <month>; categories with under 2 months of history say "Not enough history".
How do I raise a budget when a fund keeps running out?
Edit the category's amount for the month, or click Set budget in the spending-pace alert's details, which applies the suggested amount to this month. Raise the default (not just a month) if it's a permanent change.
Can I search by category code?
Yes — type a 3-digit prefix like 029 for a whole group's totals and per-line progress bars, or a 4-digit code for one line.
💰Paycheck Budgeting
What is the Paycheck tab for?
A "give every dollar a job" view built around one paycheck rather than a calendar month (Budget → 💰 Paycheck). Assign what you received to expense categories and funds until nothing is left unassigned.
Generate Pay Periods vs ＋ New Paycheck Session?
Generate Pay Periods (frequency, anchor payday, typical amount) builds a year of paydays to click through. ＋ New Paycheck Session is for a one-off paycheck, listed under "Manual".
How do I assign money?
Type into a category's box (it saves as you type), use ↑Bgt to fill that category's monthly budget, Auto-Fill from Budget for all categories, or Assign Remaining to put the rest in one category. Recurring-bill chips for items due in the period fill their category in one click.
Does Save actually save?
Boxes save instantly; Save marks the session finalized (and confirms if dollars remain unassigned). Anything unassigned shows as a sidebar alert.
Can I plan a paycheck before it arrives?
Yes — use 📅 Plan a Paycheck on the Dashboard so it appears as a planned deposit that doesn't count until payday.
🔁Recurring Transactions
What frequencies are supported?
Weekly, Biweekly, Monthly, Yearly and Custom (every N days). The Funds page normalizes them to a monthly cost.
Post vs Skip?
Post creates the transaction and advances the due date; Skip advances without creating one (you paid it elsewhere or it didn't occur). On mobile, the Recurring tab has Post to Ledger.
How do I see what's due?
A red badge on Recurring shows the count; due items sit at the top of the page; the Dashboard header shows a "Due" pill; sidebar alerts flag overdue and due-this-week bills.
What's the 📊 Timeline view?
A 6-month forward projection of every active recurring item — scheduled in vs out per month and a dated list of each occurrence.
Why do recurring items matter for fund alerts?
A payee that matches an active recurring item is treated as a bill: it's reserved for when due and excluded from the "spending too fast" pace. Keep your recurring list accurate so only everyday spending triggers those alerts.
📈Reports
How do I change the period?
Use ‹ › to step through months, click the month label for a calendar, or the dropdown (This Month, Last 3/6 Months, This Year, Custom Range).
What reports are there?
Income vs Expenses (6 months), Income Breakdown, Spending by Category, Spending Heatmap, Money Flow, This Period vs Last Year, Data Health Check, Account Balance Trends and the Transaction Statement.
What does Spending by Category show?
Your top 10 expense categories for the period with dollars and share of total (toggle This Period / Year to Date); splits count toward the correct category.
What are the Spending Heatmap and Money Flow?
The Heatmap shades each day of the month by spending (darker = more) so weekday/weekend and paycheck-week patterns stand out. Money Flow shows income splitting into top categories and whatever's left as Saved.
What is "This Period vs. Last Year"?
It shifts your selected range back one year and lists the biggest category movers (e.g. "+18% Dining"). If last year's month was frozen it uses that locked number. Hidden for Custom Range.
What does the Data Health Check flag?
Categories with no transactions ever, accounts inactive for 90+ days, uncategorized spending, and payee names that look like the same merchant spelled differently ("Amazon" vs "AMAZON.COM").
What does category group search show?
Searching 029 shows the group's total actual vs budget with per-line progress bars; 0291 shows one line.
How do I export a PDF?
Click ⬇ Export PDF: a new tab opens with an executive summary, budget vs actual, income breakdown (if logged), top categories and the full statement — print or save as PDF.
💳Debt Payoff
How do I see which transactions I've paid off on a card?
On the Debt Payoff page, click the ▶ next to a debt that's linked to a credit-card or loan account. You'll see what you owe now, what was charged and paid in the last 90 days, interest and fees, a month-by-month table, and every transaction with a running Owed after balance. Payments are applied to the oldest charge first (like a card statement), so each charge is marked ✓ Paid, ◐ partly paid or ● Open, and a dashed line shows where you're paid down to. Payments made by transfer show which account they came from, and the next scheduled payment from Recurring is listed. Click any row or Open in Transactions to jump to that account's full ledger.
What strategies are available?
❄ Snowball — extra to the smallest balance first. 🏔 Avalanche — extra to the highest rate first (least total interest). Minimums Only — the baseline.
How does Extra Monthly Payment work?
It's added to your total minimums and applied to the target debt per the strategy; everything recalculates as you type.
Are balances connected to my accounts?
Yes. Credit and Loan accounts are imported automatically, and a debt linked to an account (the Linked Account selector) syncs its balance each time you open the page.
How can I see which transactions paid a debt down?
Once linked, any deposit you record on that account (a card or loan payment) automatically pays the debt down. Click ▶ in the debt row to expand Payments linked to… and see each date, payee and amount.
What does the Interest Comparison show?
Your chosen strategy vs minimums-only: total interest and months to debt-free. The difference is what you save.
🧾Income Breakdown & Tax Tracking
What is the Income Breakdown popup?
After saving a deposit (or applying a replenishment) you can log Gross Amount and deduction lines (Federal Tax, State Tax, Social Security, Medicare, custom). Net is filled from the deposit; a warning shows if Gross − Deductions ≠ Net.
How do I view or edit one?
Transactions with a breakdown show a green 💰; click it for the gross/deducted/net view and Edit Breakdown.
Where does it show up in Reports?
The Income Breakdown report totals gross, deductions, net, effective tax rate and a per-line table (e.g. total Federal Tax year to date).
📓Journal
What is the Journal for?
A dated, searchable notebook for context numbers can't hold — decisions, follow-ups, wins. It's separate from the one-line Memo on a transaction.
How do I add and find entries?
Use the Quick Note box (optionally a tag — 📝 Note, 🔔 Follow-up, 💡 Decision, 🎯 Goal, 📊 Review, 🏆 Win — and a linked transaction) then Save →, or ＋ New Entry for longer ones. The header search covers text, tags and linked transactions.
What is the Weekly Review?
The 📋 Weekly Review button in the sidebar (plus a Sunday prompt) summarizes the week: income, expenses and net, top categories, month budget pace vs time elapsed, bills due in the next 7 days and flagged items.
☁️Sync & Data Safety
Where is my data stored?
In your browser's localStorage on this device; nothing is sent anywhere unless you set up sync. The app works offline.
How do I back up?
Open ☁️ Sync Data, enter a GitHub personal access token (gist scope) and a Gist ID, then push manually or turn on Auto-Sync (3 seconds after a change). Do it at least weekly — clearing browser data without a backup loses everything. A small dot on the mobile Home screen is green when auto-sync is fully configured.
How do my phone and computer stay in step?
Push from one device and pull on the other through the same Gist. Make changes on one device at a time and push before switching.
How are changes saved?
Edits save after a 400 ms pause (the "Saving…" indicator shows at once). Balances and fund numbers refresh immediately when you save.
Can I password-protect it?
Yes — set, change or remove a password under ☁️ Sync Data → 🔒 App Lock (also offered on a brand-new file). It's a soft lock for casual privacy, not encryption, and there's no recovery: forgetting it means erasing all data.
How do I open the Setup Wizard again?
Click ⚙ Setup Wizard at the bottom of the sidebar. It won't erase data; changes save when you click Finish & Launch.
How do I start completely fresh?
☁️ Sync Data → ⚠️ Danger Zone → Clear All Data — Start Fresh, then type DELETE. This is permanent — push a backup first.
🛠Troubleshooting & Glossary
A transaction isn't showing in my fund.
It needs to be tagged with that fund or be in the fund's Linked Category. Transfers ignore category matching and need an explicit fund (or a fund on the split lines). Check the Fund column, and that the transaction isn't a not-yet-posted planned one.
Why is a fund's balance different from the account it lives in?
They measure different things. An account is real money; a fund is the part of it earmarked for a purpose. One account usually holds several funds' money — that's what the account pills and Unallocated amount show.
What does Unallocated mean?
The part of an account's balance that no fund claims (account balance − the sum of every fund's share in it). A large amount means money that hasn't been given a job; a negative one means funds have been assigned more than the account holds.
My planned paycheck isn't in my balance.
That's by design — planned items count only once their date arrives, then post automatically.
A fund went negative — what now?
It's been given less than it's spent. Move money in from another fund (Transfer Between Funds), contribute to it, or raise its budget. The sidebar's details panel suggests which.
I made a transfer between funds but my bank balance didn't change.
Correct — fund transfers are virtual. Use ⇄ Add transfer to record real movement between accounts.
The numbers looked out of date right after I saved.
Older versions refreshed balances up to a moment after saving; the current version updates immediately. If anything looks stale, reload the page.
The app feels slow.
Big histories are handled by showing 200 transactions at a time, and by caching balances. Use filters or Load 200 more, and avoid keeping hundreds of rows expanded.

☁️ Sync Data — GitHub Gist

Backup and sync your Meridian data across devices
How this works: Your data is saved as a private file on your GitHub account (called a Gist). Only you can see it. To sync between devices, open Meridian on each device and paste the same token and Gist ID.

One-time setup: Create a free GitHub account, then generate a personal access token with Gist permissions. Takes about 2 minutes. See the instructions below.
This is stored only in your browser's localStorage and never sent anywhere except GitHub's own API.
📖 Step-by-step setup instructions ▶
Step 1 — Create a GitHub account
Go to github.com and sign up for a free account if you don't have one. Confirm your email.

Step 2 — Generate a Personal Access Token
1. Click your profile picture (top right) → Settings
2. Scroll all the way down → click Developer settings
3. Click Personal access tokens → Tokens (classic)
4. Click Generate new token → Generate new token (classic)
5. Give it a name like "Meridian Sync"
6. Set expiration to "No expiration" (or however long you want)
7. Check the gist checkbox — that's the only permission needed
8. Click Generate token at the bottom
9. Copy the token immediately — GitHub only shows it once. It starts with "ghp_"

Step 3 — Paste the token above and click Push to Cloud
Leave the Gist ID blank on your first sync. Meridian will create a new private Gist automatically and show you the ID to save.

Step 4 — Set up on your other devices
Open Meridian on your phone or another computer. Paste the same token and the Gist ID that was created in Step 3. Click Pull from Cloud to load your data.
